title: No circle, no regress: faith reduces to an authority received immediately by the Spirit's illumination
source_text: XXXIX. Namque ut istud inculcem quod satis notari non potest, in fidei probationibus, nec potest dari circulus, nec progressus in infinitum, quorum utrumque est vehementer absurdum: adeoque fides nostra necessario reducitur ad aliquam authoritatem, cujus testimonium ut divinum, adeoque ut sincerum & incorruptum suscipimus, propter se & immediate, per illuminationem internam Spiritus sancti, qui eo nos adducit, non amplius externo aliquo, alterius divini verbi testimonio, sed alius generis motivis & incitamentis.
pass_a_gloss: For that I may inculcate that which cannot be noted enough, in the proofs of faith, neither can a circle be given, nor a progress to infinity, each of which is vehemently absurd: and so our faith is necessarily reduced to some authority, whose testimony we receive as divine, and so as sincere and uncorrupted, for its own sake and immediately, through the internal illumination of the Holy Spirit, who leads us there, no longer by some external testimony of another divine word, but by motives and incentives of another kind.
pass_b_english: In faith's proofs neither circle nor infinite regress is allowed — both are absurd.
Faith must reduce to some authority received as divine (and thus sincere) for its own sake and immediately.
The Holy Spirit's internal illumination brings us there — not by another external divine word's testimony, but by motives of another kind.
